name: Gallery One dawn pass
note: "Admit bearer. Before the public. After the police. — P." Both, ideally.

name: Wrong-pattern mounting screw
note: Fresh burr, wrong slot. Swapped, not forced. Hung by someone who loved it. That narrows things wonderfully.

name: 1926 acquisition file
note: Sale via V. Casal, consignor a trust. Sixty thousand crowns. A miracle with a receipt.

name: Blotter telegram draft
note: "DR. LORENTZ — POSTPONE EXAMINATION — DISCRETION ESSENTIAL — A.V." What examination? And why does discretion cost extra?

name: Cradle blueprint, O. Marsh 1905
note: Whoever swapped the frame could read this drawing blind.

name: 1907 nightingale clipping
note: "…the Belmont's nightingale, Miss Marsh, who sings to the paintings at night…"

name: 1904 harbor chart
note: The harbor as the painter saw it. No North Mole. Filed under 'obvious', eventually.

name: Pawn ticket No. 77
note: BRASSBOUND PAWN, QUAYSIDE — one brass sextant — 40 cr. It fell out of the frame's lie.

name: Pawn ledger, item 77
note: Pledged T. FINCH — redeemed 12 Oct., cash, new notes. Pawned in shame, redeemed in a hurry.

name: The Chalk's slate
note: "T.F. — 40 — PAID 12 OCT." Paid in exactly the shape of his debt. Somebody knew his number to the crown.

name: Berth ledger
note: A painting-sized crate to the SS Vesper, berth 9, dawn after the theft.

name: SS Vesper lading slip
note: One crate, 140 × 110 × 30 — consigned 'V.C. FINE ARTS'. A name the exact size of a suspect.

name: Finch's duplicate log book
note: He rewrote an hour of his life. The hour has other witnesses.

name: Forged customs stamp, 9 kg
note: An empty crate, stamped like a full alibi — with Casal's name pinned to the sheet.

name: Hotel register
note: Casal, Suite 412, resident. Dr. E. Lorentz arriving Oct 20 — booked by the Belmont, attn. A. Voss.

name: Casal's genuine stamp die
note: Brass, worn, a nicked serif on the C. His mark, but not his die. Someone stamped his name onto a lie.

name: Deciphered cipher ledger
note: Keyed entries: prior lots brokered for the same voice. He has dealt with 'Nachtigall' before.

name: Drop note & grey glove
note: No words — a lattice sigil and FRIDAY. The glove is a signature or a slip. With her, I'd bet signature.

name: Telegram signed NACHTIGALL
note: "LATTICE STALL. FRIDAY. BRING THE 1926 FILE." The voice signs its name. Friday, then.

name: Dead-drop slip
note: "No more meetings. The wren flies too close." I've been called worse, by fonder people.

name: Pigment order book
note: 1904 materials, no modern colors — for E. SARTO, 6 Kestrel Lane. Somebody is painting in 1904, twenty-three years late.

name: Freight waybill, Oct 11
note: 23:15, museum spur → Clocktower Lane siding. Retired-staff pass No. 7. The painting went uphill, not to sea.

name: Pounced cartoon fragment
note: The Daughter's hands, pricked line by line. This is how you copy a masterpiece — or rebuild one.

name: Vane-green pigment pot
note: "GRÜN — E.V." in a steady old hand. Copper resinate in beeswax. Dead men don't buy linseed.

name: Lot 9 — the 1904 study
note: Same girl. Same room. Different harbor. One of these paintings has been somewhere the other hasn't: the future.

name: Consignment ledger — Aurelia Trust
note: Sell everything, no reserve, bearer bonds by month's end. Nobody liquidates a life unless the life is about to change address.

name: 1919 minute: 'seal not recovered'
note: Conservator O. MARSH relieved of duties… seal never surrendered. Somewhere, it's still stamping.

name: Aurelia 1913 manifest
note: "E. VANE — boarded" — without the purser's countermark. The drowning that wasn't.

name: Sarto's sketchbook
note: A recent sketch: an older woman, the nightingale brooch. Drawn from life. With love. The dead have better eyesight than advertised.
caption: Die Nachtigall singt noch · El ruiseñor todavía canta · L'usignolo canta ancora — "The nightingale still sings."

name: Duplicate 1926 dossier
note: Consignor AURELIA TRUST, correspondence: 9 CLOCKTOWER LANE. Cartographers kept chart rooms up there. Cartographers — and their daughters.

name: Original stretcher bar, E.V. 1904
note: Fresh tack holes. The original never left this tower until now. She isn't hiding it anymore. She's moving it.

name: Finch's transfer papers
note: The nightingale-watermark seal, retired 1921, 'not recovered'. The theft signed itself.

name: Telegraph counterfoil 'O.M.'
note: HOLD CABIN — SELENE — PIER 4 — PASSENGER O.M. She's never hidden. We just kept looking at louder things.

name: The nightingale brooch
note: "For the wren. I'm going home." She wore it in 1904. She's carrying the painting back up the hill.

name: The retired seal itself
note: Brass and nightingale, discarded at the foot of the hollow frame like a returned key. The Broker retired tonight.

name: The case, closed
note: Every pin connected, none dangling. Filed under: home.
